conventions: bpp = Mbps*1e6/(W*H*fps) of the recorded file resolution; fixed = codecs whose bitrate does not scale with resolution/fps choice

cameras.name: Panavision Millennium DXL2
cameras.notes: Panavision Millennium DXL2 (2018): RED MONSTRO 8K VV sensor (40.96x21.60 mm, 8192x4320), Light Iron Color 2, firmware V-1.0.0 manual (2020). Records R3D (REDCODE RAW, 2:1-22:1 target ratio; camera falls back to next achievable ratio), R3D + ProRes, R3D + DNxHD/HR, ProRes only, or DNxHD/HR only, to Panavision MINI-MAG 512GB/1TB. Panavision spec: max 60 fps 8K FF, 75 fps 8K 2.4:1; 'up to 1 hour on a single magazine'. Other max fps taken from RED DSMC2 MONSTRO spec (same sensor/DSMC2 platform) and marked; null where unknown. REDCODE bpp uses RED's 14-bit Recording Time tool model (estimated - DXL2 not in tool). Media throughput assumed like RED MINI-MAG (300 MB/s) - not stated by Panavision. Anamorphic formats (2x 6:5, 1.3x, 1.25x) share pixel dims of spherical formats. Available through Panavision rental only.

resolutions.name: 8K 6:5 (2x anamorphic)
resolutions.note: pixel dims per RED MONSTRO 8K 6:5; DXL2 manual lists 8K 6:5 under Anamorphic 2x without dimensions

codecs.name: REDCODE 2:1
codecs.ref: bpp = 14/2 (RED Recording Time tool model for MONSTRO 8K VV: MB/s = W*H*14/8*fps/ratio/1e6). DXL2 is not in RED's tool; Panavision manual: DXL2 uses the RED MONSTRO 8K VV sensor, records R3D (REDCODE RAW) with target ratio 2:1 (lowest) to 22:1 (highest) selectable, to Panavision MINI-MAG 512GB/1TB. Same model reproduces RED DSMC2 MONSTRO published minimum ratios at 300 MB/s (8K FF 24fps 5:1, 60fps 12:1).

codecs.name: ProRes 4444 XQ
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE: Panavision does not publish ProRes data rates (manual refers to Apple's ProRes data rates); Apple ProRes White Paper (Apr 2022) 24p targets: 2k-ff 453 Mb/s (bpp 8.5336). DXL2 manual: ProRes is scaled from any format to 4K or 2K; 4K ProRes up to 60 fps (ProRes only) or 29.97 fps with simultaneous R3D; R3D + ProRes not supported in 4K FF format. Flavor-by-resolution availability (4444/XQ only at 2K) assumed from the RED DSMC2 MONSTRO platform - the DXL2 manual text does not list ProRes flavors; DXL2 4K proxy width (4096 vs 3840) not confirmed.

cameras.name: Phantom Flex4K (incl. Flex4K-GS)
cameras.notes: Vision Research Phantom Flex4K / Flex4K-GS: 9.4 MP S35 sensor (27.7x15.5 mm, 6.75 um), 64 or 128 GB RAM. Two recording paths: loop mode into RAM at full speed (then saved/offloaded to CineMag IV), or run/stop direct to CineMag IV / IV PRO (1TB/2TB) at lower rates (raw 4K up to ~120 fps per record table; ProRes up to 136 fps on CineMag IV PRO). Storage = frames captured x bytes/frame, so for high-speed shots compute from captured frames (not playback duration). Max fps per resolution from the data sheet (2048x1152 = 1900 from record table; key features list 2048x1080 @1975). No published Mb/s; bpp derived from Vision Research record-time tables and statements (estimated). Cine RAW can be transcoded to ProRes/H.264 in PCC (not in-camera recording). Flex4K-GS adds global shutter (same data).
sources: https://www.phantomhighspeed.com (Phantom Flex4K Data Sheet Rev March 2017; copy used: https://w-technika.cz/cdn/shop/files/dsflex4k.pdf)

codecs.name: Phantom Cine RAW (uncompressed, 12-bit)
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE (derived): Vision Research calls Flex4K Cine Raw 'uncompressed'; sensor is 12-bit (VEO4K family data sheet, same sensor/platform), so 12 bits/pixel packed = W*H*1.5 bytes/frame. Checked against Flex4K data sheet 'Maximum Record Times': 128GB RAM 4096x2304 @938 fps = 10 s (model: 128 GiB/(4096*2304*1.5 B) = 9706 frames = 10.3 s); 4096x2160 @1000 = 10 s (model 10.4 s); 2TB CineMag IV PRO run/stop 4096x2160 @24 = 120 min (model: 2 TiB = 115 min; 2 TB = 105 min); 4096x2304 @120 = 22 min (model 2 TiB: 21.6 min). Exception: data sheet 2048x1152 @500 = 40 min raw on 2TB is ~2x the 12-bit model (20 min) - unexplained, likely a data-sheet inconsistency. Bits/pixel not explicitly published.
codecs.source: https://www.phantomhighspeed.com (Phantom Flex4K Data Sheet Rev March 2017; copy used: https://w-technika.cz/cdn/shop/files/dsflex4k.pdf)

codecs.name: ProRes 422 HQ
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE (derived from Vision Research figures): ProRes 422 HQ only at 4096x2304 and 2048x1152 (CineMag IV recording). Data sheet: 'files become 2.5X smaller compared to an equivalent Cine Raw' -> 12/2.5 = 4.8 bpp; record-time table 4096x2304 @120 fps = 55 min on 2TB CineMag IV PRO -> 2 TiB/(120*3300 frames) = 5.553 MB/frame = 4.71 bpp (4.28 bpp if 2 TB decimal). Using 4.71. The table's 2048x1152 @500 = 100 min implies ~half that (same anomaly as raw). Up to 938 fps in loop mode (RAM), up to 136 fps run/stop to CineMag IV PRO (original CineMag IV: 30 fps). For comparison, Apple's white-paper 422 HQ target is ~3.55 bpp at 4096x2160.
codecs.source: https://www.phantomhighspeed.com (Phantom Flex4K Data Sheet Rev March 2017; copy used: https://w-technika.cz/cdn/shop/files/dsflex4k.pdf)

cameras.name: Phantom VEO 4K (VEO4K-PL / 990 / 590)
cameras.notes: One entry for the VEO4K family (models 990S, 990L, 590S, 590L, 4K-PL; later PL-RLS). Same 9.4 MP 12-bit S35 sensor (6.75 um, global + rolling shutter), RAM 36 or 72 GB (4K-PL: 72 GB standard), records to RAM then saves Cine RAW to CFast 2.0 (S and PL models; L model via Ethernet only). Differences: 990 and 4K-PL = 9 Gpx/s (4096x2304 @938, 4096x2160 @1000, 2048x1080 @1970); 590 = 5 Gpx/s (4096x2304 @500, 4096x2160 @550, 2048x1080 @950) - per-model max fps in resolution entries (maxfps = 990/PL). 4K-PL adds cinema-style black housing, OLPF and PL mount; L = software-controlled body; S adds on-camera controls, I/O and CFast. Record time @max fps with 72GB: 5.6 s (990/PL 4K) / 10 s (590 4K); 36GB halves it. CFast save speed from RAM 90 MB/s. No in-camera ProRes - Cine RAW only (ProRes/H.264 via PCC transcode). Storage = frames captured x bytes/frame.
sources: https://www.phantomhighspeed.com (Phantom VEO4K Family Data Sheet Rev August 2017; copy used: https://w-technika.cz/cdn/shop/files/dsveo4kfamily.pdf)

codecs.name: Phantom Cine RAW (12-bit)
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE (derived): data sheet: custom 9.4 MP 12-bit CMOS, native file format Phantom Cine RAW (.cine); 12 bits/pixel packed = W*H*1.5 bytes/frame. Cross-check with data sheet 'Example Frame Rates & Record Times' (72GB RAM, 990/4K-PL, binary GiB): 4096x2304 @938 fps 5.6 s -> 12.48 bpp; 4096x2160 @1000 fps 5.6 s -> 12.48 bpp; 4096x1152 @1850 fps 5.6 s -> 12.65 bpp; 2048x2048 @1050 fps 11 s -> 12.77 bpp; 2048x1152 @1850 fps 11 s -> 12.88 bpp; 2048x1080 @1970 fps 11 s -> 12.90 bpp - i.e. 12 bpp plus a few % RAM overhead/rounding (using decimal GB gives ~7% lower). No Mb/s published.
codecs.source: https://www.phantomhighspeed.com (Phantom VEO4K Family Data Sheet Rev August 2017; copy used: https://w-technika.cz/cdn/shop/files/dsveo4kfamily.pdf)
